params.body:
## Why

`stocklist:fotos-afgeleid` runs every five minutes and its queue was a silence. Nothing outside the
command knew how many photos still lack their derived sizes, so a failed `ProcessVehiclePhoto`, a
queue worker that was down for a night, a Blurit webhook that changed the bytes or a nightly import
could keep pushing photos back onto the PHP route without anything saying so. The pages keep
working, which is exactly why nobody would notice.

The scheduler comment also said the line could go once everything had a `media_version`. That is
wrong on purpose now: the sweeper is permanent, because the queue keeps refilling.

## What

- `App\Support\DerivedPhotoBacklog` holds the selection in one place: eligible photos (not deleted,
  a path, done processing, a vehicle that still exists) whose derived sizes are missing
  (`media_version` null) or of an older generation (`media_set` null or below
  `VehicleImageService::SET`). Photos marked as missing (`media_version` 0, the file is not in the
  bucket) are not backlog; `--opnieuw` retries those. The command's own `teDoen()` now starts from
  the same base, so the two cannot drift apart.
- The command ends every run with what it did and what is left, both for its own selection
  (`--tot-wagen`, `--wagen`, `--shard`) and for the whole fleet, and writes the fleet number away so
  the next reader can see a trend.
- `/api/elixir` reports it under `extra.photos.withoutDerivedSizes` (plus `derivedSet` and
  `lastSweepAt`) through `App\Elixir\PhotoPipelineProbe`, declared in `config/elixir.php` as a class
  name rather than a closure, because `config:cache` does not serialise closures.
- `stocklist:smoke photos` is one line: the number, and whether it went down since the last sweep.
  A backlog is not a failure, so the line is always green and the exit code stays 0.
- The scheduler comment says why the line stays and what `--tot-wagen=20710` is for; `CUTOVER.md`
  gets the step that removes that boundary after the fresh media delivery, with one `--opnieuw` run.

## Query cost

One `COUNT(*)` with the same where clauses, no ordering and no join to `vehicles` beyond the
existence check. `vehicle_photos` had no index on either media column (only `vehicle_id`,
`processing`, `processed_uuid`), so the migration adds `vehicle_photos_media_index` on
`(media_set, media_version)`: the predicate is a range on the leading column and the second column
is read from the same index. The endpoint caches the number for 60 seconds, which is shorter than
the five minutes between sweeps, so a poll never costs more than one count per minute.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='DerivedPhotoBacklog|IntegrationSmoke|VehicleImageRoute|RouteCache|DemoMedia|ClassReferencesResolve|HealthRoute'` against local MySQL `forge_test`, green.
- New `tests/Feature/DerivedPhotoBacklogTest.php`: the count holds exactly the two outstanding
  states and excludes the current, the missing, the still-processing, the deleted photo and the
  photo of a deleted vehicle; the rows the command actually touches are the rows the count named;
  the endpoint exposes the number; the smoke line prints it and reports the trend.
- `BuildStampTest` fails in a git worktree (`.git` is a file there, so there is no checkout to read)
  and is unrelated to this change.
params.title: Photos: the derived-size backlog becomes a number instead of a silence
